# Check CHK-010 — Vulnerability, Support Needs and Foreseeable Harm Overlay

Case: ABC-99    Tenant: 99
Regulatory basis: PRIN 2A.2.1R; PRIN 2A.5; PRIN 2A.6; FCA FG21/1

## The check
Where the Suitability Report includes details of needs and adjustments or duty of care resulting from client vulnerabilities, are they consistent with the evidence provided?

*Wherever we assess the appropriateness of recommendations (through all the prompts) they should consider any characteristics of vulnerability that the client may have and any needs and adjustments that have been agreed in the evidence provided.

### What to look for
Consistency:
- Details of additional support and needs, including where third party support has been requested
- Communication preferences and formats 
- Adjustments to support client comprehension
Appropriateness (overlay):
 - Vulnerability has a material impact on the recommendation

### Decision logic
No Issue: evidence complete, consistent and supports outcome. 

Potential Concern: material clarification or additional evidence required. 

N/A: trigger absent.

## Trigger
Canonical model checkTriggers.hasVulnerabilityIndicators = false. 16 corroborating passage(s) from 2 probe search(es).
The trigger appears absent; say so if the evidence below bears that out.

## How to decide
- No Issue: Vulnerability was assessed and recorded, any characteristics found are reflected in the report's description of support needs, communication and adjustments, and the recommendation accounts for them.
- Potential Concern: Indicators exist in the file that the report never reflects, support arrangements are asserted without evidence, or no vulnerability assessment appears anywhere in a case carrying clear drivers.
- N/A: Rarely applicable — this check is an overlay on all cases. Use N/A only where the case type places it out of scope entirely.

Severity guidance:
- Highest: a recorded vulnerability that materially affects suitability and is absent from the report's reasoning.
- High: no vulnerability assessment anywhere in a case with clear FG21/1 drivers (health, life event, low resilience, low capability).
- Moderate: support needs recorded in the file but not reflected in the report's communication or adjustments.
- Low: communication preferences captured but not referenced in the report.

Overlay: After deciding this check, revisit the appropriateness limbs of CHK-002 to CHK-009 with any identified characteristics in scope. A recommendation that is appropriate for a resilient client may not be appropriate for this one.

## Death
Once we receive written notification of death and a certified copy of the death certificate, we will confirm to the personal representative what our requirements are to allow us to take instructions from them.  Once these requirements are met, we will be able to take instructions from the personal representative and this agreement will become binding on them. We will stop ongoing service fees as soon as feasibly possible having been notified of the client's death.  Any ongoing fee that has been received up to that point can be considered to cover the work financial advisers may be requested to carry out.  If additional work is required or if ongoing fees have not been received a time-based fee may be charged.

## Your current situation
You are currently aged 69 and married to Kim, aged 65. You are both in good health and have three grown-up children, all of whom are financially independent. You work full-time as an HGV driver through an agency, typically earning around £300 per week net, with additional income of £20 per week from your volunteer role with the Sea Cadets. Kim earns approximately £1,100 per month net. You are in receipt of your full State Pension of £230 per week, and Kim will receive her full State Pension of around £230 per week when she reaches State Pension age. You expect to retire within the next two years, while Kim intends to continue working until she reaches 66, at which point she plans to retire fully.
Your current household expenditure is approximately £1,700 per month, covering rent, utilities, food, transport, entertainment, and insurance. You hold savings of around £6,000 and have no outstanding liabilities, providing a secure financial base. You also hold several pension arrangements with a combined value of approximately £110,000, which form the basis of your retirement provision. You have contacted me to review your position for retirement, seeking guidance on consolidating your pensions and ensuring your income and assets meet your future needs.
You have confirmed that you retain sufficient liquid capital to cover any unexpected emergencies, giving you reassurance as you progress with your retirement planning.

## 2. Active Oversight and Governance
 Our CIP is actively monitored and reviewed by an experienced investment committee.
 This ensures that the portfolio remains aligned with market conditions and your risk profile, providing greater adaptability compared to a static multi-asset fund.
## 3. Cost Efficiency
 The CIP is structured to balance performance and cost, optimising value for your investment.
 While individual multi-asset funds may offer simplicity, the CIP's layered approach can enhance performance without excessive costs.
The CIP aligns with your long-term goals and offers a more robust and flexible framework compared to a single multiasset fund. It provides enhanced oversight, risk management, and adaptability, ensuring that your investment remains effective as market conditions and personal circumstances evolve.
## Investment pathways
Investment pathways were introduced in February 2021 by government legislation. The legislation is designed to ensure that individuals who take benefits from their pension fund via drawdown without taking advice still have access to appropriate investments for their needs and objectives.
There are four investment pathways to cater for four retirement scenarios. The four pathways are:
 Option 1 - I have no plans to touch my money in the next 5 years.
 Option 2 - I plan to use my money to set up a guaranteed income (annuity) within the next 5 years.
 Option 3 - I plan to start taking my money as a long-term income within the next 5 years.
 Option 4 - I plan to take out all my money within the next 5 years.
The provider will offer a single investment solution designed to meet each option. Although investment pathways are aimed at individuals that do not have an adviser, they may still be a valid consideration for you because they may have:
 Potentially lower costs;
 Reduced complexity; and
 Less requirement for ongoing advice.

## Your client can get 24/7 access to their pension at MyAviva

Your client can look at their plan online 24/7. They can keep track of their pension and most other policies they have with us, in one secure and convenient place, at myaviva.co.uk .

They can check their life insurance policy, find car insurance documents and even view pension statements from previous years. Registering for MyAviva is quick, and it's completely free. It's just one of the ways we're making life easier for our customers.

## What if your client doesn t want to keep making payments?

They can still keep the pension money built up in this pension with us (until age 75).

Plan number: SP50163762

<!-- page: 5 -->

## What if your client doesn t want to keep making payments?

We ll still manage the plan and continue to send yearly statements. They'll stay invested in their chosen funds (unless we're told to change them) and the value of the plan will go down or up depending how these funds perform. Just be aware that we will continue to take charges from the plan (details of these will be in the statements). Also remember that the effect of inflation and any charges will reduce how much pension money is worth over time. Alternatively, your client can transfer the pension money to another provider if preferred.

Your client s pension money has to stay in a pension until they at least reach the minimum pension age. This is currently age 55 (57 from 6 April 2028). However, depending on their circumstances they may be able to access their pension pot earlier such as when they have a protected pension age (to find out more visit aviva.co.uk/nmpa ) or are unable to work due to ill health or incapacity.

## Your client s retirement options

Income Drawdown

Taking the fund as a cash lump sum, known as a full/partial UFPLS (Uncrystallised Funds Pension Lump Sum)

Annuity income

Open Market Option Moving funds to drawdown is available for this plan from age 55 (57 from 6 April 2028). We allow ad hoc payments to be taken, but don t offer a regular withdrawal facility.

Moving to income drawdown isn t possible after age 75. But once funds have been moved to income drawdown, the money can remain invested for the rest of life.

**Risk profile**
########### This section details how we reached an agreed risk level for this goal. It covers factors including your natural attitude to risk, capacity for loss and required return; factors used when selecting the types of investments and determining suitability.
**How are risk levels used to create suitable investment portfolios?**
The natural risk level, which is ascertained from the psychometric attitude to risk questionnaire score, is used as a starting point to discuss the actual level of risk you are willing and able to take to meet your specific investment objective.
In the discussion we had, you were shown a projection, based initially on your natural risk level, investment amount, target and desired time horizon. We then discussed this projection and altered any factor, including the risk level, until we agreed that the right balance had been achieved. This resulted in an agreed risk level for the investment.
To project the potential outcomes, each risk level is mapped to a collection of asset classes designed to expose you to an appropriate level of risk. Projections are produced by passing the asset class breakdown for the selected risk level to a stochastic engine that uses modelling provided by Hymans Robertson to project the future performance of the combination of asset classes.
By using these projections and discussions, we came to an agreed risk level for your specific investment objective. A portfolio will be built to meet your agreed risk level.
A summary of the results of this process is documented below.
Natural risk level
Your natural risk level is based on the answers given in the Attitude to Risk Questionnaire which was completed on 18/09/2025. The responses can be found in the appendix

#### How to compare
Method: NarrativeAlignment
- Guard: Age alone is not vulnerability; combine it with reliance, health or capability indicators before concluding.
- Guard: Where vulnerability is genuinely absent and that has been assessed and recorded, the overlay adds nothing — say so rather than manufacturing a concern.

#### If evidence is missing
- Evidence absent: Where the report asserts no vulnerability but nothing in the file shows it was considered, treat the assertion as unsupported.
- Both absent: Where no vulnerability assessment exists anywhere in the case, record that as the finding — the overlay was never applied.
